match.front: What is the net force on a dipole in a uniform external field, and what does it experience instead?
match.back: The net force on the dipole is zero, since E is uniform. However, the charges are separated, so the forces act at different points, resulting in a torque on the dipole.

match.front: Define the electromotive force (emf) of a source.

questions.stem: If the number of turns in a coil is tripled, the value of the magnetic flux linked with the coil:

match.front: Formula: flux linkage N1Φ1 of solenoid S1 due to current I2 in solenoid S2, which defines the mutual inductance M12
match.back:
When a current I 2 is set up through S2, it in turn sets up a magnetic flux through S1. Let us denote it by Φ1. The corresponding flux linkage with solenoid S 1 is
N 1 Φ1 = MI 12 2
M 12 is called the mutual inductance of solenoid S 1 with respect to solenoid S2. It is also referred to as the coefficient of mutual induction.
match.source: NCERT, Physics Part I, chapter 6, page 166
